title.narrative: Provision of emergency and sustainable life-saving WASH response packages to drought affected people in Burhakaba district in Bay region

description.narrative: ltpgtIn November 2025, Somalia officially declared a state of drought emergency, highlighting the severity of the crisis and the urgent need for scaled-up humanitarian assistance. The prolonged and recurrent drought has triggered an unprecedented humanitarian emergency, with an estimated 4.4 million people projected to face acute food insecurity between October and December 2025. Among those affected are approximately 1.85 million children suffering from acute malnutrition, including 421,000 at risk of severe acute malnutrition (SAM).ltbrgtThe crisis is compounded by a critical lack of access to safe and reliable water, which worsens malnutrition, heightens vulnerability, and fuels disease outbreaks. According to Somalia WASH Cluster, over 3.1 million people lack access to safe drinking water at the moment, contributing to ongoing outbreaks of cholera, acute watery diarrhea, and measles, particularly in drought-affected rural areas.ltbrgtTo address these urgent needs, the GRRN project will support life-saving WASH objectives by improving access to safe water and promoting hygiene practices in the most drought-affected communities of Burhakaba rural villages. Key interventions include:ltbrgt Rehabilitation of 8 strategic shallow wells equipped with hand pumps, serving approximately 3,000 direct beneficiaries.ltbrgt Emergency water trucking for 12,000 drought-affected people (3,720 women, 3,000 men, 2,700 girls, and 2,580 boys), ensuring immediate access to safe water for drinking and domestic use, purchase and installation of 4 water bladders, construction of two berkadsltbrgt Water quality assurance measures, implemented by GRRN’s dedicated team (one Water Quality Supervisor and two Water Quality Monitors) to conduct routine water testing, inspect water trucks, and ensure systematic chlorination of water sources.ltbrgt Establishment and training of 8 Water Management Committees (WMCs) to promote sustainable operation, maintenance, and community ownership of rehabilitated water sources. construction of 35 emergency latrines which 15% are latrines with disability features and each household will be provided with portable solar lamps to ensure equitable access to sanitation facilities to the drought displaced communities, conduct 15 clean up campaigns to ensure safe living, learning and working environment for the affected communities in Buur Hakabalt/pgtltpgt Purchase and Distribution of 2000 hygiene kits targeting most vulnerable households in the targeted settlements.ltbrgt Comprehensive hygiene promotion activities, including community campaigns, household sessions, and targeted trainings to reduce waterborne diseases and encourage safe hygiene practices.ltbrgtThrough these integrated interventions, GRRN will address immediate life-saving needs while building community resilience, mitigating public health risks associated with drought and strengthening community capacity for sustainable water management.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
